messages:
maria: Heads-up — running long-context perf runs on qwen-34b-mqa and noticed sustained memory growth over ~30k tokens. Not typical fragmentation, looks like repeated page churn during KV eviction sweeps. attaching quick profile below (pasted).

kai: Can you paste the profile? is this on dedicated infra or hosted?

maria: Dedicated repro on gc-ssd pool. Minimal churn until ~12k tokens then mmaps spike. profile snippet:
```
alloc_count: 12 -> 430 per step after 12k
mmaps: 0 -> 18 (background sweep triggers)
kv.pages_in_use: 1024 -> 1487
kv.page_size: 64MB
worker kernel: prefer-large-kernels=true
```

pranav: hmm. we've seen MQA's rope scaling cause mis-aligned KV segments which prevents reuse across batches. The sweep is freeing partial pages but then kernel selection picks large-gemms that assume contiguous KV layout -> more allocations.

zach: so kernel selection + sweep timing interacting badly. can you repro with prefer-small-kernels?

maria: tried prefer-small-kernels=false and true; small kernels reduce transient cpu but memory growth still there, just delayed. suspect paging granularity.

kai: question — are we evicting by LRU at token granularity or by page? If LRU evicts tokens across pages we fragment pages and cause mmaps.

maria: eviction is page-based but we have a background sweep that compacts only when free_pages > threshold. It seems compaction isn't triggered because free fragment sizes are < page_size but > block_size. result: many small free blocks inside pages.

pranav: possible fix: increase low-watermark for compaction or run occasional aggressive compaction at cohort boundaries (eg. when rope-scale factor increases). Also consider aligning MQA KV block allocator to page_size boundary.

kai: quick experiment: bump kv.page_size 64MB -> 128MB and set sweep_interval=10s (was 30s), run a 50k token tf run. results?

maria: did that. memory growth flattened, mmaps count stabilized at 3, tail latency unchanged. But cost: larger reserved pages so slightly higher baseline memory.

zach: tradeoff seems acceptable for Dedicated customers. For Hosted we could make this dynamic per-model: MQA models get larger page_size + more aggressive sweep.

infra-bot: Note: created ticket INF-8721 to track kv-allocator changes and kernel-selection flag gating per-model.

pranav: also add a quick perf test: sequence of increasing rope scalars with MQA/Qwen and assert mmaps < 5. add to nightly infra-run.

maria: opened PR with patch to align allocator and an env var REDWOOD_KV_PAGE=128M to test. will post benchmarks tomorrow.

kai: nice. if you can capture flame graphs showing kernel change events vs alloc spikes that'd help ops approve. :thumbsup:

maria: on it, thanks!
